thread:
maria: saw a p99 spike hitting hosted-api-prod around 3411112222, p95 up too. Notified by dashboards :alarm_clock:

sachin: on it. metrics look like a sharp jump in queue_depth and concurrent inflight requests to the text-gen route. any deploys?

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T09:10Z by sam to runtime/kselector-service (rev: d4f7a2)

lee: that deploy touched sampler heuristics + kselector thresholds earlier today. could be related.

maria: timeline aligns. spike ~5m after deploy. p99 ~2.2s -> 6.8s. p95 ~400ms -> 1.8s. throughput steady but tail is bad.

sachin: initial quick checks: no obvious host-level CPU/GPU saturation, memory fine. but batch fill rates dropped to ~30% for many shards. looks like sampler underfills small short prompts.

maria: can we confirm kernel selection logs? kselector might be switching to fallback kernel which is slower for small batches.

lee: pulled kselector logs from one affected shard, here's the tail: ```
[09:14:12] kselector: selected=fp16-vec-kernel reason=latency_predict miss_count=1
[09:14:14] kselector: selected=fallback-slow-kernel reason=kernel_mispredict confidence=0.12
[09:14:14] runtime: kernel_switch_count=1
```

sam: aha, confidence low -> immediate fallback. that fallback has higher per-token latency at small batch sizes. why mispredict? maybe sampler's feature vector changed after heuristic tweak.

nina: I grabbed a flamegraph from one affected GPU process, big hump in fallback-kernel::compute():```
  [flamegraph snippet] fallback-kernel::compute  62%
  batching::dispatch 18%
  kcache::lookup 10%
```

maria: kv-cache hit rates? if prefix cache misses go up, we see more KV IO and longer latency.

lee: KV cache hit-rate dipped from 91% -> 74% concurrent with spike. but sampler changes shouldn't directly evict cache. maybe more short queries invalidating prefetch usage.

sachin: ran a quick profiler on the sampler thread. sampled 1k requests: feature vector distribution shifted: avg_seq_len dropped (23 -> 12 tokens) and variance increased. our training for kselector expected distribution centered ~22.

maria: lower sequence length + small batch fill likely changes kernel perf curve; kselector threshold uses historical throughput/latency mapping and mispredicted.

sam: temporary mitigation ideas: 1) pin kselector to avoid fallback for specific model routes 2) force sampler to prefer slightly larger batch windows (add 10ms) 3) revert today's sampler tweak.

lee: suggestion 2 is lowest risk. increasing target coalescing latency by 10ms should increase batch fill to ~60% based on sim. want to patch config and roll to 10% traffic first.

maria: agree. do we have an experimental canary?

infra-bot: Rolling config change to 10% shards: kselector.coalesce_ms += 10 -> (applied to shards: shard-4, shard-9, shard-12)

sachin: after canary, p99 on canary shards dropped back to ~2.6s within 2 minutes, batch fill -> 58%, kernel selection stabilized to fp16-vec-kernel. good signal.

maria: excellent. schedule cluster-wide rollout? we should also capture a postmortem note: root cause = sampler heuristic drift causing shift in request feature distribution -> kselector misprediction -> fallback kernel selection -> p99 spike.

lee: I'll open a quick PR to make kselector's decision robust to short-sequence heavy tails (add smoothing and fallback debounce). tagging sam for revert plan if needed.

sam: I'll prepare a rollback of the sampler tweak if the config roll doesn't hold. also adding an eval job that simulates short-seq traffic to catch regressions.

nina: added dashboards for 'kselector_mispredict_rate' and 'batch_fill_by_seq_len' and an alert at 5% mispredict rate sustained 2m.

maria: action items: (1) propagate coalesce_ms +10 across all shards (sam to monitor) (2) PR to harden kselector (lee) (3) add regression eval (sam) (4) postmortem doc (maria). We'll reconvene after 1h to confirm stability. :thumbsup:

sachin: current aggregate p99 back to ~2.4s cluster-wide after 15m. will watch.

maria: thanks team. adding incident label and starting notes for postmortem.
